gate2_calibration.note: No threshold per spec; Opus is the reference tier. Reference-tier inter-seat pattern-exact agreement is 0.467, i.e. the coding vocabulary is itself only moderately reproducible at the reference tier.

gate3_parity.method: per-tier 2-seat consensus (places = intersection of the two seats, falling back to seat A when the intersection is empty; verb = seat A on disagreement) compared to the Opus consensus built the same way. pattern string = sorted(places)+'>'+verb.
gate3_parity.ruling: NO TIER CERTIFIES. Sonnet consensus vs Opus consensus: 0.133 pattern-exact, 0.672 mean Jaccard. Haiku consensus vs Opus consensus: 0.000 pattern-exact, 0.444 mean Jaccard. Both fall far below the 0.80/0.90 gate. Per the spec ('No tier certifies -> bulk runs on Opus; say so, don't stretch'), P4 BULK runs on Opus.

gaps: P1 note: the OpenAI Model Spec yields ~50 authority-tagged behaviour sections; to hold the corpus inside the spec's 60-100 target a seeded subsample of 29 was taken with random.Random(20260857) over the extracted section order. All other sources taken in full except Anthropic constitution (12 of ~50 CAI principles, picked to avoid near-duplicates) and Anthropic Usage Policy (10 of ~90 universal-standard bullets, spread across categories). Selection code: scratchpad/build_corpus.py.

P3 seat incident: Haiku seat A did not appear to have written its output within the coordinator's polling window and was re-dispatched once per the re-dispatch rule; the original dispatch then completed (~98s) and had in fact written a valid 15/15 coding. The ORIGINAL first-dispatch coding was snapshotted and restored as the seat of record, and the retry's overwrite was discarded. No gap in coverage.

P3 finding (not a spec gate): Opus inter-seat pattern-exact agreement on the calibration sample is only 0.467, so the low cheap-tier parity numbers partly reflect vocabulary under-determination rather than tier capability alone. Surfaced, not acted on.

P4: tripwire fired (0.615 > 0.20 pattern disagreement on the seeded spot-check). Coding artefacts are complete but uncertified; P5 should not be run on them without the spec owner ruling on the vocabulary under-determination described in tripwire.diagnosis_for_the_spec_owner.

p4_bulk.reason: No tier certified at GATE-3; spec directs bulk to Opus.
p4_bulk.batching: 85 remaining definitions split into committed batch packets of 25/25/25/10; each batch a separate blind seat dispatch per seat.
p4_bulk.machine_check: all 8 bulk batch files and the spot-check file passed coverage and value-legality; 0 problems, 0 re-dispatches needed in P4.

tripwire.rule: P4 spot-check pattern disagreement > 20% -> halt, surface.
tripwire.detail: The independent Opus spot-check seat agreed with the two-seat bulk consensus on the exact pattern string for only 5 of 13 sampled definitions (0.385 pattern-exact; 0.615 disagreement), against a 0.20 ceiling. Verb agreement was high (0.923); the disagreement is almost entirely in places_constrained (mean Jaccard 0.756).
tripwire.action: HALTED. P4 coding artefacts are complete and committed, but the bulk codings are NOT certified as a stable basis for P5 saturation/richness estimation. Escalated rather than improvised around.
tripwire.diagnosis_for_the_spec_owner: This is consistent with the GATE-2 reading: two independent Opus seats on the calibration sample agreed pattern-exact only 0.467 of the time, and on the 85-item bulk only 0.482. The frozen coding vocabulary under-determines places_constrained (which 1-3 of 10 places a definition 'constrains' is not pinned by the definition text alone), so pattern-string identity is noisy at EVERY tier including the reference tier. A saturation/richness estimate over pattern strings inherits that noise directly. The cheap-tier parity failure at GATE-3 is therefore only partly a tier-capability result.
